questions.title: Reverse the Array
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void reverse_array(int arr[], int n)

It must reverse the first n elements of arr in place. The harness prints the array afterwards.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n reversed values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Minimum and Maximum
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void min_max(int arr[], int n, int *mn, int *mx)

It must store the smallest value into *mn and the largest into *mx. The harness prints both.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum, then the maximum, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Second Largest Element
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int second_largest(int arr[], int n)

It must return the second largest DISTINCT value in the array (the largest value strictly smaller than the maximum). The array is guaranteed to contain at least two distinct values.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the second largest distinct value.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Sum and Average
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void sum_average(int arr[], int n, int *sum, double *avg)

It must store the total into *sum and the mean (sum / n as a double) into *avg. The harness prints the sum and the average rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the sum, then the average rounded to 2 decimals, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000

questions.title: Count Occurrences of K
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_key(int arr[], int n, int k)

It must return how many of the n elements equal k.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value|, |k| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Byte Offset of an Index
questions.description:
Contiguous arrays place element i at byte offset i * sizeof(int). The scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long byte_offset(int index)

It must return the byte offset of element index in an int array, computed with sizeof.

Input Format:
One line with the index.

Output Format:
One line with the offset in bytes.

Constraints:
0 <= index <= 10000

questions.title: Cold Storage Warmest Shelf
questions.description:
A cold-storage warehouse logs the temperature of each shelf. The control panel shows the warmest reading and the first shelf (0-based) that holds it.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void hottest_shelf(int arr[], int n, int *val, int *idx)

It must store the maximum value into *val and its FIRST 0-based index into *idx. The harness prints both.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum value, then its first index, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Canteen Token Rotate Left
questions.description:
The canteen token board is redrawn each hour: every token moves one place to the left and the first token wraps around to the last position.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void rotate_left(int arr[], int n)

It must shift the n values left by one position in place (arr[0] moves to arr[n-1]). The harness prints the array afterwards.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n values after the rotation, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Lab Sensor Spike Count
questions.description:
A lab sensor grid logs readings along a line. A reading is a "spike" when it is strictly greater than both of its immediate neighbours (interior positions only).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_spikes(int arr[], int n)

It must return the number of spikes (0 when n < 3).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the spike count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Attendance Register Dedup
questions.description:
A duplicated attendance register must be trimmed: keep the FIRST occurrence of every roll number and drop later repeats, preserving order.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int dedupe(int arr[], int n)

It must compact arr in place to keep only first occurrences and return the new length. The harness prints the new length, then the trimmed values on a second line.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
Line 1: the new length. Line 2: the trimmed values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Insert Value at Position
questions.description:
A course waitlist stores roll numbers in an array. When a new student is admitted at position pos (0-based), every element from pos onward shifts one slot right.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int insert_at(int arr[], int n, int pos, int val)

It must insert val at 0-based position pos (0 <= pos <= n), shifting the tail right, and return the new length n + 1. The harness prints the updated array.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: pos and val.

Output Format:
One line with the n + 1 values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, 0 <= pos <= n, |value|, |val| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Delete Value at Position
questions.description:
When a student drops a course, the waitlist closes the gap: every element after position pos (0-based) shifts one slot left.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int delete_at(int arr[], int n, int pos)

It must remove the element at 0-based position pos (0 <= pos < n), shifting the tail left, and return the new length n - 1. The harness prints the updated array.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (n >= 2). Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: pos.

Output Format:
One line with the n - 1 remaining values, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 10000, 0 <= pos < n, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Shifted Sorted Check
questions.description:
A patrol route list is an ascending array of distinct checkpoints that was rotated left by some amount (possibly zero). Verify the rotation: the array is a rotated sorted array exactly when it has at most one "descent" — a position where arr[i] > arr[i+1] — counted circularly (the wrap from the last element back to the first).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_rotated_sorted(int arr[], int n)

It must return 1 when the array is a rotated ascending array of distinct values, else 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated distinct integers.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Matrix Bytes Report
questions.description:
A graphics buffer is declared as int grid[rows][cols]. Contiguous row-major layout means the whole grid occupies rows * cols * sizeof(int) bytes and a single row occupies cols * sizeof(int) bytes.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void matrix_bytes(int r, int c, long long *total, long long *rowbytes)

It must store the total grid bytes into *total and the single-row bytes into *rowbytes (computed with sizeof). The harness prints both.

Input Format:
One line with r and c.

Output Format:
One line with the total bytes, then the row bytes, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 1000

questions.title: Move Zeros to End
questions.description:
A parking sensor feed records slot occupancy as ints; the maintenance report pushes every 0 reading to the back while keeping the relative order of the non-zero readings (a stable partition).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int move_zeros(int arr[], int n)

It must rearrange arr in place so all non-zero values (in their original order) come first and all zeros follow, and return the count of non-zero values. The harness prints the full rearranged array.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the n rearranged values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Merge Two Sorted Halves
questions.description:
An attendance sheet of even length n is split at h = n / 2 and BOTH halves are already sorted ascending. The registrar merges them into one fully sorted array.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void merge_halves(int arr[], int n)

It must merge the two sorted halves in place so the whole array is ascending. The harness prints the merged array.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (even). Line 2: n space-separated integers (each half sorted ascending).

Output Format:
One line with the n merged values, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 10000, n is even, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Second Smallest and Second Largest
questions.description:
A tournament analyst reports the "runner-up" stats of a score sheet: the second smallest DISTINCT value and the second largest DISTINCT value. The sheet always has at least two distinct values.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void second_extrema(int arr[], int n, int *smin, int *smax)

It must store the second smallest distinct value into *smin and the second largest distinct value into *smax. The harness prints both.

Input Format:
Line 1: n (n >= 2). Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the second smallest, then the second largest, space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Remove All Occurrences of Key
questions.description:
A shipment manifest is scrubbed: every entry matching a rejected batch key is removed and the rest close ranks, keeping order.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int remove_all(int arr[], int n, int key)

It must delete every element equal to key, keep the remaining order, and return the new length (possibly 0). The harness prints the new length, then the remaining values on a second line.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: key.

Output Format:
Line 1: the new length. Line 2: the remaining values, space-separated (an empty line when none remain).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value|, |key| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Leader Elements Scan
questions.description:
A relay team sheet lists split times; a split is a "leader" when it is strictly greater than every split to its right (the last split is always a leader).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int leaders(int arr[], int n, int out[])

It must fill out with the leaders left-to-right and return their count. The harness prints the leaders.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the leaders, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, |value| <= 1000000000

questions.title: In-Place Circular Rotate
questions.description:
A signal buffer must rotate LEFT by k positions using ONLY in-place swaps (the reversal trick: reverse the first k elements, reverse the rest, reverse the whole array). No extra array is allowed.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void rotate_reversal(int arr[], int n, int k)

It must rotate the n values left by k (k may exceed n; reduce it modulo n). The harness prints the rotated array.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the n rotated values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000, 0 <= k <= 1000000000, |value| <= 1000000000
